packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-09 - unverified blind image reading (reader D)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification or earlier reading of this fragment was in my
  context.
- Beyond the brief: I made greyscale contrast-boosted 2x enlargements (upper
  and lower halves) of tiles 002-005 and 007-010 in my scratchpad folder
  (readerD/). To find the image files without listing the directory I probed
  image-NNN.jpg names in sequence (found 001-010). No other files opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: one face of a long horizontal parchment strip, c. 30 x 6 cm,
  with a modern white number "15 7370?" / "K 7370?" written at the left end.
  image-006: the other face (held flat with glass rods).
- The strip was cut ACROSS a leaf: text lines run along the strip. Several
  columns of very small, dense gothic text are visible side by side,
  separated by ruled intercolumns (pale vertical bands): on face 1 at least
  four column blocks (left of c. 6 cm, c. 10, c. 14, c. 17 cm on the ruler
  scale) - tentatively the strip spans more than one page (e.g. a
  conjugate pair or a bifolium folded), but this is uncertain.
- A horizontal fold / crease with slits runs the full length about 2/3
  down; text on both sides of it.
- c. 20-24 lines visible per column; tiny script, heavy abbreviation, brown
  ink much faded and stained. No coloured initials or rubrics seen. Some
  words appear underlined or overlined (possibly lemmata or headings;
  tentative). Paragraph marks / spaces before "Ad primum", "Ad secundum"
  are visible (image-004).
- Tiles: 002-005 cover face 1 left to right; 007-010 cover face 2. Tiles
  overlap their neighbours at the edges.

SELECTED SPANS
I chose the best-preserved block, the column in image-004 (face 1, third
block), and read it fully as far as possible; I add short readings from
image-002 and image-008. Other blocks remain largely unread.

TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: (x) expansion; x? uncertain; [..] [illegible]; line numbers
count from the top of the named tile (lines cut by the top edge counted).

  l.26  [..] s(ecundu)m materia(m) corp(or)is? h(ec) (?) (com)plexionis . S(ed) h(ec) dispo(sitio) talis? .  Ad [..]
  l.27  [..] q(uod) (com)plexio n(on) e(st) for(ma) (com)plexionis? . S(ed) e(st) accide(n)talis? tal(is)? .  It(em) no(n) e(st)

  NB l.14-17 of image-004 lower half repeat l.13-16 of the upper half in my
  enlargements; counted once above.

image-004.jpg - narrow block at far right (line beginnings of next column)
  scattered: "ui(us)?", "nil?", "(con)tra?", "col(or)?", "a ob[..]", "colo[..]"
  - too fragmentary to transcribe connectedly.

image-002.jpg - left block, sample lines (counted from tile top)
  l.12  [..]trar(ium)? / [..] (?) d(icitu)r (?) ra(tio)ne? [..] ad (con)tra? (?) gr(adu)s?
  l.15  [..] ut? [..] sic? (com)p(lexio)? [..] ap(er)i(t)? (?)olt? [..] uni(us)? (?)
  l.20  [..] sem(per)? toti(us)? (?) loco? h(ic)? d(icitu)r? . (com)plexio? [..]
  (rest of block [illegible] at this resolution)

image-008.jpg - face 2, central block, sample lines
  l.6   [..] (com)p(ar)ata? . [..] q(ui)? (?) . [..] qualitas? (?) ita? [..]
  l.7   [..] (?) . G(e)n(er)alit(er)? [..] uirtutes? [..] (?)ue? [..]
  l.8   [..] (?) ex (?) aliq(ui)d? . [..] alia? a(n)i(m)a? [..]
  l.12  [..] (?) qualitas? (con)traria? [..] qualitat(is)? (?)
  l.13  [..] ut? (?) colo(rem)? (?) (et) cu(m)? [..] (?) sic? (?) . (?) d(icitu)r? (?) . [..] a q(uo)? [..]
  (rest [illegible])

SELECTED / UNREAD
- Read: image-004 central column (most of c. 27 lines, with many uncertain
  words). Recurring and fairly secure: "(com)plexio", "for(ma)
  (com)plexionis corp(or)is", "Ad p(ri)ma(m) ...", "Ad s(ecundu)m
  d(icendu)m q(uod) ... e(st) duplex . Vna", "accide(n)talis",
  "dispo(sitio)". These suggest a scholastic question with replies to
  arguments (Ad primum / Ad secundum / Ad tertium) - an interpretation, not
  an identification.
- Mostly unread: the column blocks in image-002, 003, 005 (face 1) and all
  of 007, 009, 010 (face 2); only samples given above.

LIMITATIONS
- The script is extremely small; the tiles are at the edge of legibility.
  Higher-resolution capture (and raking light for the creases) is needed
  for a full reading of the remaining columns.
- Column order across the strip and which face is the outer side are
  unknown. Overlap between neighbouring tiles was not exhaustively mapped.
